tools.name: ask_1c_ai
tools.title: Ask the 1C:Naparnik assistant
tools.description:
Ask a free-form question to the 1C:Naparnik AI assistant.
Use this tool for any 1C-related question that does not fit the specialised tools:
general 1C development advice, architecture questions, explanations of concepts,
syntax clarification, or anything else about the 1C:Enterprise ecosystem.

IMPORTANT: Unlike all other tools (which always start a fresh discussion), this tool
reuses the caller's own most recent discussion by default. Reuse is scoped to the
caller: a discussion is never shared with another user, project or task. Set
create_new_session=True to start from scratch when switching topics.

For code checking use check_1c_code, for style review use review_1c_code,
for documentation search use search_1c_documentation / its_help.

create_new_session.description: If True, starts a fresh discussion discarding previous context. If False (default), reuses this caller's own latest discussion.

files.description:
Paths to source files to attach to the question as context. Give a path
relative to the repository root the server has mounted (e.g.
CommonModules/Модуль/Ext/Module.bsl) or an absolute path inside a directory
named by ONEC_AI_WORKSPACE_ROOTS (in the container: /workspace/...). The
server runs in its own container, so a path on your own machine (a
drive-letter path, /home/...) is not visible to it unless the operator
declared that prefix in ONEC_AI_WORKSPACE_PATH_MAP. Read only; a path outside
the declared directories is refused, and a deployment that set nothing
refuses every path.

tools.name: check_1c_code
tools.title: Check 1C code for errors
tools.description:
Basic check of 1C:Enterprise code — syntax errors, logical issues, and performance problems.
Use this tool for a technical correctness check: will the code compile, are there bugs,
are there N+1 queries or other performance anti-patterns.

In direct mode the upstream syntax capability produces both the syntax result and the
logic-and-performance analysis within a single discussion. When that capability is not
available, or the call does not succeed, the answer comes from the prompt path and the
result carries a machine-readable `fallback_reason` saying which capability was
concerned and what state it resolved to.

For style/standards compliance, use review_1c_code instead.
For an AI-proposed rewrite of the code, use rewrite_1c_code instead.

files.description:
Paths to read the code from instead of passing it inline. Prefer this for
anything large: the server reads the file, so nothing is lost assembling the
argument. Give a path relative to the repository root the server has mounted
(e.g. CommonModules/Модуль/Ext/Module.bsl) or an absolute path inside a
directory named by ONEC_AI_WORKSPACE_ROOTS (in the container: /workspace/...).
The server runs in its own container, so a path on your own machine (a
drive-letter path, /home/...) is not visible to it unless the operator
declared that prefix in ONEC_AI_WORKSPACE_PATH_MAP. Read only; a path outside
the declared directories is refused, and a deployment that set nothing
refuses every path. Give either code or files, not both.

tools.title: Review 1C code style and standards
tools.description:
Review 1C:Enterprise code for style, standards compliance, and best practices.
Use this tool for a quality/style review: naming conventions, code structure,
compliance with 1C development standards (ITS), readability, and recommendations.

ONEC_AI_TOKEN validity. This tool always uses the prompt path.

tools.name: rewrite_1c_code
tools.title: Propose an AI rewrite of 1C code
tools.description:
Get an AI-proposed rewrite of 1C:Enterprise code, returned as a reviewable proposal.

The result is data, not an instruction: it carries a hash of the exact source you
supplied, a byte-faithful diff from that source to the proposal, and a validation
status drawn from the closed set `passed`, `failed`, `not_performed`, `unavailable`.
A status other than `passed` is reported honestly — the prompt asks the model to
validate, and a request is not a guarantee.

This server applies nothing. Application is the caller's responsibility, and only
against a source whose hash equals `original_hash`, and only when `safe_to_apply`.

goal.description: Optional goal for the rewrite (e.g. 'optimize', 'readability', 'error handling')

files.description:
Paths to read the code from instead of passing it inline. Give a path
relative to the repository root the server has mounted (e.g.
CommonModules/Модуль/Ext/Module.bsl) or an absolute path inside a directory
named by ONEC_AI_WORKSPACE_ROOTS (in the container: /workspace/...). A path
on your own machine (a drive-letter path, /home/...) is not visible to the
server unless the operator declared that prefix in
ONEC_AI_WORKSPACE_PATH_MAP. Read only. Give either code or files, not both.
Naming exactly one file passes it through verbatim, so that file's
`text_sha256` in `sources` equals `original_hash` and the diff applies to it
unchanged.

outputSchema.description: Предложение по изменению кода как рецензируемый артефакт.

tools.name: modify_1c_code
tools.title: Modify 1C code by instruction
tools.description:
Modify 1C:Enterprise code according to an explicit user instruction, returned as a
reviewable proposal.

Unlike rewrite_1c_code (where the AI decides what to improve), this tool does exactly
what you tell it to. If no code is supplied the call is a generation, and the result
says so rather than reporting a hash of an empty string.

The prompt asks for syntax validation, but the result reports what was actually
observed: `passed` and `failed` only from an observed validation result,
`not_performed` when validation was possible but nothing was observed, and
`unavailable` when the syntax capability is not available.

This server applies nothing.

Search 1C:Enterprise platform documentation.
Use this to find information about built-in language methods, platform objects,
types, events, properties, and general platform capabilities.
For general queries use phrases like 'Общая информация о ...', 'Список всех ...'.

A configured default documentation version is used when none is given, supplied by
the ONEC_AI_DOC_VERSION setting, and it can be overridden per call. The version that
actually answered is reported in `version_used`; the server does not track "latest"
and does not claim to.

tools.name: its_help
tools.title: Search the ITS knowledge base
tools.description:
Search the 1C ITS (Information Technology Support) knowledge base.
Use this tool to find methodological recommendations, technical articles,
configuration documentation, standards, and best practices published on ITS.

Results are returned as structured records. Each record carries `id`, `title` and
`snippet`, and the `id` is directly acceptable to fetch_its — there is nothing to
parse out of prose. A record is built from the upstream tool result: from its
machine-readable details, or from the ITS document addresses that result itself
carries, an identifier being derived from an address by one fixed rule. `title`
and `snippet` are filled only where upstream supplied them.

An empty `records` with `structured_records_available` true means upstream searched
and found nothing. Where only a prose answer was available, `records` is empty and
`structured_records_available` is false. Identifiers are never read out of the
answer text, so an identifier mentioned there never becomes a record.

outputSchema.description: Результат поиска по базе знаний ИТС.

tools.name: fetch_its
tools.title: Fetch an ITS document
tools.description:
Fetch the content of a specific ITS document, catalogue or database by its identifier.
Typically used after its_help, passing the `id` field of a returned record.

The identifier is validated for shape before any upstream request. An identifier
matching none of the recognised forms — `root`, `superior`, `v8std`, `its-...-hdoc`,
`its-...-hdir`, `its-...-buh30` — fails as a malformed-identifier error and no request
is issued. A well-formed identifier upstream cannot resolve is reported as a not-found
condition, which is a different problem with a different remedy.

result carries a machine-readable `fallback_reason`.

tools.name: config_help
tools.title: Search 1C application documentation
tools.description:
Search documentation for a specific 1C:Enterprise application (configuration).
Use this to find information about objects, modules, registers, documents, catalogs,
and business logic of a specific 1C application — such as "Бухгалтерия предприятия",
"ERP", "Управление торговлей", "ЗУП", etc.

This searches application-level documentation. Use search_1c_documentation for
platform-level documentation (language, objects, types).

If config_name is empty, the server uses the default from the ONEC_CONFIG_NAME setting.
